The Takatso SAA Deal - what is going on?

By: Hein Kaiser | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we ask why SAA can be sold for R 51 after costing taxpayers billions

Unique Selling Point:
SAA has cost taxpayers billions, it holds assets of billions and yet government is selling it to Takatso for R 51.

Summary:
SAA is being sold by Public Enterprises for Takatso for R 51 - that is after it worked out that the R 3bn in working capital, to be injected over 3 years, is equal to an independent analysis of SAA's value. Yet, 2 months ago SAA stated in a dated response that it estimates its assets to be worth R 10bn. That's a massive difference.

There are so many unanswered questions - and there is a withdrawn Scopa presentation by Treasury that reveals a whole lot more.

Further information:
Takatso gets SAA debt free, sans any liabilities. Airlink's law suit for R 800m is a liability to the taxpayer as govt is taking all historial liabilities into public purse.

Meanwhile Treasury, in the leaked and 'withdrawn' Scopa presentation questions why DPE should receive preferential shares in SAA (the golden shares) In addition Treasury said: Terms of the working capital agreement with the SEP are not outlined in the documents provided by DPE to NT. Therefore, it is not clear whether funding from the SEP will be advanced to SAA in the form of debt, equity or a hybrid instrument. This implied that the SEP, may assume very minimal shareholder risk for the acquisition of a majority shareholding at the purchase price of R51.

It seems the whole deal is shrouded in mystery and a measure of skulduggery. (Scopa Presentation In CB posession)


In addition, Mango's sale is also a mess. and funding has been going to and fro - its business rescue practitioner forced to take legal steps to recover bailout funding. It's missed deadlines and is at a standstill, thanks to DPE.

Press Release:


Selling SAA
South African Airways was once the crown jewel in the aviation industry. But something went terribly wrong and for years, taxpayers have been forking out billions to bail the airline out of financial turmoil. Now, a majority share in the airline is being sold to a private consortium for what some experts believe may be a fraction of its value. So, how much is our embattled national airline really worth? Well, depending on who you ask, it’s as much as R10 billion. So why has it been sold off for a mere R 51 and then R3 billion in promised operating capital? Carte Blanche crunches the numbers. Producer: Hein Kaiser | Presenter: Masa Kekana

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): we ask why SAA can be sold for R 51 after costing taxpayers billions
metadata.Unique Selling Point: SAA has cost taxpayers billions, it holds assets of billions and yet government is selling it to Takatso for R 51.
metadata.Summary: SAA is being sold by Public Enterprises for Takatso for R 51 - that is after it worked out that the R 3bn in working capital, to be injected over 3 years, is equal to an independent analysis of SAA's value. Yet, 2 months ago SAA stated in a dated response that it estimates its assets to be worth R 10bn. That's a massive difference. There are so many unanswered questions - and there is a withdrawn Scopa presentation by Treasury that reveals a whole lot more.
metadata.Further information: Takatso gets SAA debt free, sans any liabilities. Airlink's law suit for R 800m is a liability to the taxpayer as govt is taking all historial liabilities into public purse. Meanwhile Treasury, in the leaked and 'withdrawn' Scopa presentation questions why DPE should receive preferential shares in SAA (the golden shares) In addition Treasury said: Terms of the working capital agreement with the SEP are not outlined in the documents provided by DPE to NT. Therefore, it is not clear whether funding from the SEP will be advanced to SAA in the form of debt, equity or a hybrid instrument. This implied that the SEP, may assume very minimal shareholder risk for the acquisition of a majority shareholding at the purchase price of R51. It seems the whole deal is shrouded in mystery and a measure of skulduggery. (Scopa Presentation In CB posession) In addition, Mango's sale is also a mess. and funding has been going to and fro - its business rescue practitioner forced to take legal steps to recover bailout funding. It's missed deadlines and is at a standstill, thanks to DPE.
